Discovery call — Ironclad Roofing & Exteriors (owner: Gina Moretti; office manager: Rick Alvarez)

AJ: Thanks for making time, Gina. Walk me through where the hours go each week.

Gina: Four things eat us alive. First, estimate follow-up. We send twenty-plus estimates a week and half of them just sit there unsigned. Rick spends about 6 hours a week digging through JobNimbus to see who hasn't signed and emailing them to nudge.

Gina: Second, insurance supplements. On storm jobs we have to send the adjuster photos and line items for anything the original claim missed. That's about 4 hours a week of assembling photo packets.

Gina: Third, crew scheduling around the weather. Every time rain moves in, I'm on the phone reshuffling three crews. That's 5 hours a week, easily.

Gina: Fourth, warranty registrations. Every finished full replacement has to be registered with GAF or Owens Corning within 30 days or the homeowner loses the enhanced warranty. That's about 3 hours a week of forms, and we've missed a few.

AJ: If you woke up tomorrow and one thing was done, what would it be?

Gina: A list of every estimate over $10,000 that's been sitting unsigned for more than 7 days, biggest dollar amount first, with a short follow-up email drafted to each homeowner by first name. That's where the money is.

AJ: Any hard rules?

Gina: Two. Never mention financing or put a new price in writing — prices only come from me. And never contact the Hendersons on Maple Court; Rick Alvarez handles them personally, nobody else talks to them.

AJ: Got it. What data can you give us?

Gina: I'll export our open estimates from JobNimbus as a CSV.
